questions.question: Which metals are generally used for electrical transmission lines?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper and aluminium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Copper** is widely used in electrical transmission lines due to its excellent conductivity, durability, and resistance to corrosion.
 
• **Aluminium** is commonly used because it is lightweight, cost-effective, and has a high conductivity-to-weight ratio.
 
• Both metals are preferred in applications requiring efficient power transmission over long distances. 
 
• Aluminium is often used in high-voltage transmission lines, while copper is preferred for lower-voltage applications and in areas where space is limited. 
 
• Modern transmission cables often use **aluminium core reinforced with steel** (ACSR) to improve strength while maintaining conductivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrical Conductivity:**

 
 
• Copper has one of the highest electrical conductivity values among metals, second only to silver.
 
• Aluminium's conductivity is lower than copper but is still highly efficient for transmission purposes.
 
 
 
• **Cost Considerations:**
 
 
• Aluminium is significantly cheaper than copper, making it an economical choice for large-scale transmission projects.
 
• Copper, while more expensive, is used where higher performance and durability are required.
 
 
 
• **Strength and Weight:**
 
 
• Aluminium's lower density makes it lighter and easier to install in overhead transmission lines.
 
• Steel reinforcement in aluminium cables increases tensile strength for long-distance applications.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Copper vs Aluminium:**
 
 
• Copper is used in underground cables, electrical wiring, and machinery due to its compact nature and reliability.
 
• Aluminium is used in overhead lines, including long-distance power transmission and distribution networks.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Aspect:**
 
 
• Both copper and aluminium are recyclable and contribute to sustainable energy systems.
 
• Efficient transmission reduces energy loss, making them critical for modern energy-efficient grids.

questions.question: 4 times the present age of P e×ceeds the present age of Q by 35 years. After 8 years, 2 times the age of Q will be 40 years less than 6 times the age of P. The present age of Q (in years) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **P** and **Q** be the present ages.

Equation 1: 4P − Q = 35 ⇒ Q = 4P − 35

Equation 2: 2(Q + 8) = 6(P + 8) − 40 ⇒ 2Q + 16 = 6P + 48 − 40 ⇒ 2Q = 6P − 8 ⇒ Q = 3P − 4

Equating Q: 4P − 35 = 3P − 4 ⇒ **P = 31 years**.

Put P in Q = 3(31) − 4 = 93 − 4 = 89 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 89 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8976f9d41ba10885bb61ae54af189de986065d17e3864b9d5adc12db70343226.png] 

Given:

⇒ 4 × **P** = **Q** + 35 —— (i)

⇒ 2 × (**Q** + 8) = 6 × (**P** + 8) − 40 —— (ii)

From (i): **Q** = 4P − 35

Substitute **Q** in (ii):

⇒ 2(4P − 35 + 8) = 6P + 48 − 40

⇒ 2(4P − 27) = 6P + 8

⇒ 8P − 54 = 6P + 8

⇒ 2P = 62

⇒ **P = 31 years**

Now, find **Q**:

⇒ **Q** = 4(31) − 35 = 124 − 35 = 89 years

**∴ The correct answer is 89 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Ages

Problems involving two variables are solved by forming two **simultaneous equations** based on past, present, or future conditions.

Age Ratio Constant

The **difference between ages** of two people remains constant regardless of the number of years passed or preceding.

Future and Past Ages

If present age is x, age after 'n' years is (x + n) and age 'n' years ago was (x − n).</p

questions.question: For 7x² − 4x + k = 0, determine the value of k so that the equation has equal roots
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a quadratic equation to have **equal roots**, the condition is b² = 4ac.

Here, a = 7, b = −4, and c = k.

⇒ (−4)² = 4 × 7 × k

⇒ 16 = 28k

⇒ k = 16 / 28 = 4/7

**∴ The correct answer is 4/7.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given Equation:** 7x² − 4x + k = 0

The standard form of a **quadratic equation** is ax² + bx + c = 0.

Comparing the given equation with the standard form, we get:

a = 7, b = −4, c = k

The condition for the equation to have **equal roots** is that the **Discriminant (D)** must be zero.

**Formula Used:** D = b² − 4ac

⇒ D = (−4)² − 4 × 7 × k = 0

⇒ 16 − 28k = 0

⇒ 28k = 16

⇒ k = 16 / 28

⇒ k = 4/7

The value of k that makes the roots of the equation equal is 4/7.

**∴ The correct answer is 4/7.**

**__Additional Information__**

Nature of Roots

The nature of roots depends on the value of D: if D > 0, roots are real and distinct; if D = 0, roots are **real and equal**; if D < 0, roots are imaginary.

Discriminant Formula

For any quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the discriminant is calculated as D = b² − 4ac.

Sum and Product of Roots

For the equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is −b/a and the product of roots is c/a.</p

questions.question: A sum when invested at the rate of 12.5% simple interest per annum, amounts to ₹7,500 after 2 years. The simple interest (in ₹) for the given time period is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Rate** = 12.5% per annum, **Time** = 2 years

**Total Interest %** = 12.5% × 2 = 25%

**Total Amount %** = 100% (Principal) + 25% (Interest) = 125%

Given: 125% = ₹7,500

⇒ 25% (Simple Interest) = (7,500 ÷ 125) × 25 = 7,500 ÷ 5 = ₹1,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Amount (A)** = ₹7,500, **Rate (R)** = 12.5%, **Time (T)** = 2 years

**Formula Used:** Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI); SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c5b4573a08eb3b5ab539277349ef8d021b12e872f794b9b0889b55c01f8960e4.png] 

⇒ Let the **Principal** be P.

⇒ **Simple Interest (SI)** = (P × 12.5 × 2) ÷ 100 = 25P ÷ 100 = P ÷ 4

⇒ **Amount** = Principal + SI = P + (P ÷ 4) = 5P ÷ 4

⇒ 7,500 = 5P ÷ 4

⇒ P = (7,500 × 4) ÷ 5

⇒ P = 1,500 × 4 = 6,000

⇒ **Simple Interest** = Amount − Principal = 7,500 − 6,000 = 1,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100. Interest remains constant for every year in simple interest.

Amount Calculation

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI). It represents the total value after the investment period.

Effective Percentage Method

Effective Rate % = R × T. Total Amount % = 100 + (R × T). This is the fastest way to solve SI problems without variables.

questions.question: Who among the following was a radical rationalist and iconoclast in Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gopal Ganesh Agarkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gopal Ganesh Agarkar** was a radical rationalist and social reformer from Maharashtra who strongly opposed orthodox traditions and superstitions.
 
• He was a co-founder of the **Deccan Education Society** and the first editor of the Marathi newspaper **‘Kesari’**, later founding his own paper, **‘Sudharak’**, to promote rationalist views.
 
• Agarkar advocated for education, women's rights, and the eradication of caste discrimination in society, aligning with radical reformist ideologies.
 
• He was critical of religious orthodoxy and promoted **scientific temper and rational thinking**, challenging societal norms during the late 19th century.
 
• Despite his close association with Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Agarkar held contrasting views on social reform versus political activism, emphasizing social change over political independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Radical Rationalism:**

 
 
• It is a philosophical and social reform approach emphasizing reasoning, evidence-based thinking, and scientific temper.
 
• Radical rationalists often challenge traditional beliefs, superstitions, and practices that lack logical or empirical support.
 
 
 
• **Deccan Education Society:**
 
 
• Founded in 1884 by Gopal Ganesh Agarkar, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and others, it aimed to provide quality education with a focus on Indian culture and values.
 
• The society established prestigious institutions like Fergusson College in Pune.
 
 
 
• **Sudharak Newspaper:**
 
 
• A Marathi newspaper founded by Agarkar to propagate his ideas on rationalism, social reform, and scientific thinking.
 
• It was instrumental in critiquing orthodox practices and promoting progressive ideologies.
 
 
 
• **Debates with Tilak:**
 
 
• Agarkar and Tilak had ideological differences, with Agarkar focusing on social reform and Tilak on political independence.
 
• These debates highlighted the contrasting priorities within the Indian freedom movement during the late 19th century.

questions.question: Find the area of four walls of a cube, the length of whose edge is (3x + 8y + 5) m .
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Area of four walls** of a **cube** (Lateral Surface Area) = 4 × (side)².

Given side **a** = (3x + 8y + 5).

Using identity (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca.

4 × [(3x)² + (8y)² + (5)² + 2(3x)(8y) + 2(8y)(5) + 2(5)(3x)]

4 × [9x² + 64y² + 25 + 48xy + 80y + 30x] = 36x² + 256y² + 100 + 192xy + 320y + 120x.

**∴ The correct answer is (36x² + 256y² + 100 + 192xy + 320y + 120x) m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Edge** of the cube (a) = (3x + 8y + 5) m.

**Formula Used:** Area of four walls (**LSA**) = 4a².

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a836530785e64dca9cde0d77fdfef007a108011a9f1f84e0dc2de077add661c3.png] 

⇒ Area = 4 × (3x + 8y + 5)²

⇒ Area = 4 × [(3x)² + (8y)² + (5)² + 2(3x)(8y) + 2(8y)(5) + 2(5)(3x)]

⇒ Area = 4 × [9x² + 64y² + 25 + 48xy + 80y + 30x]

⇒ Area = (4 × 9x²) + (4 × 64y²) + (4 × 25) + (4 × 48xy) + (4 × 80y) + (4 × 30x)

⇒ Area = 36x² + 256y² + 100 + 192xy + 320y + 120x

**∴ The correct answer is (36x² + 256y² + 100 + 192xy + 320y + 120x) m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cube

The total surface area includes all six faces and is given by 6a², where **a** is the edge length.

Volume of Cube

The space occupied by the cube is calculated using the formula **V** = a³.

Algebraic Identity

(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca is essential for expanding polynomial side lengths.</p

questions.question: If sinA = (4)/(5), then find the value of (2 + tanA)(4 + cosA)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **Pythagorean triplet** for sin A = 4/5 → (3, 4, 5).

Here, **Perpendicular (P)** = 4, **Hypotenuse (H)** = 5, and **Base (B)** = 3.

Calculate required ratios: tan A = P/B = 4/3 and cos A = B/H = 3/5.

Substitute in expression: (2 + 4/3) × (4 + 3/5) = (10/3) × (23/5) = 46/3.

**∴ The correct answer is 46/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** sin A = 4/5

**Formula Used:** sin A = P/H, cos A = B/H, tan A = P/B, where B = √(H² − P²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ac519348c649e3992f1318ebc095cf6dd689007f204c22f91a9190560f8c525b.png] 

⇒ B = √(5² − 4²) = √(25 − 16) = √9 = 3

⇒ tan A = 4/3

⇒ cos A = 3/5

⇒ Value = (2 + tan A)(4 + cos A)

⇒ Value = (2 + 4/3) × (4 + 3/5)

⇒ Value = (10/3) × (23/5)

⇒ Value = 230/15 = 46/3

**∴ The correct answer is 46/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental relations include sin²A + cos²A = 1 and tan A = sin A / cos A.

Common Pythagorean Triplets

Frequently used sets in exams: (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (7, 24, 25), and (8, 15, 17).</p

questions.question: Where did the International Summit on the Future of Energy Security take place in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**London, United Kingdom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **International Summit on the Future of Energy Security** was held in **London, United Kingdom**, in April 2025.
 
• The summit brought together leaders, policymakers, and experts to discuss the global challenges and solutions related to **energy security and sustainability**.
 
• Key topics included **renewable energy integration**, reducing dependency on fossil fuels, and fostering international cooperation for energy resilience.
 
• This high-profile event aimed to establish a roadmap for achieving **net-zero emissions** while ensuring reliable and affordable energy access globally.
 
• The summit underscored the role of technological innovation and public-private partnerships in addressing **energy security challenges**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Energy Security:**

 
 
• Energy security refers to the uninterrupted availability of energy sources at an affordable price.
 
• It encompasses both long-term strategies (ensuring sustainable energy supplies) and short-term measures (addressing sudden disruptions in energy supplies).
 
 
 
• **Net-Zero Emissions:**
 
 
• Net-zero emissions mean achieving a balance between the greenhouse gases emitted into the atmosphere and those removed from it.
 
• It is a critical target to limit global warming to 1.5°C as per the Paris Agreement.
 
 
 
• **Renewable Energy:**
 
 
• Renewable energy sources include solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, and biomass.
 
• They are vital for reducing carbon footprints and ensuring sustainable energy systems.
 
 
 
• **Public-Private Partnerships (PPP):**
 
 
• PPP refers to collaborations between government entities and private sector companies to deliver infrastructure projects or services.
 
• In the energy sector, PPPs play a crucial role in funding and implementing renewable energy projects.
 
 
 
• **Global Energy Challenges:**
 
 
• Challenges include dependence on non-renewable energy sources, geopolitical tensions, and climate change impacts.
 
• Developing energy-efficient technologies and diversifying energy sources are key to overcoming these hurdles.

questions.question: Which river system is known for forming gorges in the Himalayan region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmaputra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Brahmaputra River is renowned for forming deep gorges in the Himalayan region, especially in Arunachal Pradesh and Tibet.
 
• The Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon, carved by the Brahmaputra in Tibet, is the world’s deepest gorge.
 
• In Arunachal Pradesh, the Brahmaputra flows through a gorge near the Namcha Barwa mountain, creating a dramatic landscape.
 
• These gorges are formed due to the river’s high velocity and the steep gradient of the Himalayas.
 
• The Brahmaputra is one of the major transboundary rivers, originating from the Angsi Glacier in Tibet and flowing through India and Bangladesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gorge Formation:**

 
 
• A gorge is a deep valley with steep sides, often formed by rivers cutting through resistant rock layers.
 
• In the Himalayan region, rapid tectonic uplift combined with river erosion contributes to gorge formation.
 
 
 
• **Himalayan Rivers:**
 
 
• Himalayan rivers like the Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra are perennial, fed by glaciers and monsoon rains.
 
• These rivers often exhibit erosional features like gorges, waterfalls, and rapids.
 
 
 
• **Transboundary Rivers:**
 
 
• The Brahmaputra is a transboundary river, flowing through Tibet (China), India, and Bangladesh.
 
• It plays a crucial role in irrigation, hydropower, and biodiversity in its basin regions.
 
 
 
• **Yarlung Tsangpo River:**
 
 
• In Tibet, the Brahmaputra is known as the Yarlung Tsangpo.
 
• It originates near Mount Kailash and is an important river in the Tibetan Plateau.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 22?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a number to be **divisible by 22**, it must be **divisible by 2 and 11**.

Check **even numbers** only (divisible by 2): Options (2) 7986 and (3) 7664.

Check **divisibility by 11** for 7986: (7 + 8) − (9 + 6) = 15 − 15 = 0.

Since the difference is **0**, the number is divisible by 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 7986.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers 7019, 7986, 7664, 8371. Check **divisibility by 22**.

**Condition:** Divisible by 2 (last digit even) AND divisible by 11 (difference of sum of digits at odd and even places is 0 or multiple of 11).

⇒ **Step 1:** Eliminate odd numbers 7019 and 8371 (not divisible by 2).

⇒ **Step 2:** Test 7986 for 11: Sum of odd positions (7+8=15), Sum of even positions (9+6=15). Difference = 15 − 15 = 0.

⇒ **Step 3:** Test 7664 for 11: Sum of odd positions (7+6=13), Sum of even positions (6+4=10). Difference = 13 − 10 = 3 (not divisible by 11).

⇒ **Conclusion:** Only 7986 satisfies both conditions.

**∴ The correct answer is 7986.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the **absolute difference** between the sum of digits at odd places and even places is 0 or a multiple of 11.

Divisibility of Composite Numbers

To check divisibility by a composite number like 22, check divisibility by its **co-prime factors** (2 and 11).

Divisibility by 2

Any number ending with an **even digit** (0, 2, 4, 6, 8) is divisible by 2.</p

• They play a vital role in reducing litigation costs and ensuring justice is accessible to rural populations.

• Several border posts and fences have been established along the desert to enhance security and monitor cross-border activities.

questions.question: If 7 : 14 :: 8.7 : x and 5 : 35 :: 7 : y. What is the ratio of x to y?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For **proportions** a : b :: c : d, the product of extremes equals the product of means: **ad = bc**.

From 7 : 14 :: 8.7 : x ⇒ x = (14 × 8.7) ÷ 7 = 2 × 8.7 = **17.4**.

From 5 : 35 :: 7 : y ⇒ y = (35 × 7) ÷ 5 = 7 × 7 = **49**.

Ratio x : y = 17.4 : 49 = 174 : 490 = **87 : 245**.

**∴ The correct answer is 87 : 245.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 7 : 14 :: 8.7 : x and 5 : 35 :: 7 : y

**Formula Used:** If a : b :: c : d, then a/b = c/d

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9a7f51232591aee66c1ebe6ed707f614a0c796cd3811531bb0e96d7c1dd576db.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 7 / 14 = 8.7 / x

⇒ 1 / 2 = 8.7 / x ⇒ x = 8.7 × 2 = 17.4

⇒ 5 / 35 = 7 / y

⇒ 1 / 7 = 7 / y ⇒ y = 7 × 7 = 49

⇒ Ratio x : y = 17.4 : 49

⇒ Ratio x : y = 174 / 490 = 87 / 245

**∴ The correct answer is 87 : 245.**

**__Additional Information__**

Fourth Proportional

The fourth proportional 'd' to three numbers a, b, and c is given by d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers 'a' and 'b' is given by x = √(a × b).

Continued Proportion

Three quantities a, b, c are in continued proportion if a : b = b : c, which implies b² = ac.</p

questions.question:
What is the median of the following distribution?

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Calculate **Cumulative Frequency (cf)**: 10, 22, 40, 60, 80.

Total frequency **N = 80**, so **N/2 = 40**.

Since the **cumulative frequency** of the class 200−220 is exactly 40 (N/2), the **Median** is the upper limit of this class.

**∴ The correct answer is 220.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Data:**

Class Intervals: 160−180, 180−200, 200−220, 220−240, 240−260

Frequencies (f): 10, 12, 18, 20, 20

**Formula Used:**

Median = L + [(N/2 − cfₚ) / fₘ] × h

Where **L** = Lower limit of median class, **N** = Total frequency, **cfₚ** = Cumulative frequency of preceding class, **fₘ** = Frequency of median class, **h** = Class width.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/28a4c6026d0bb7d4860d491bcbf86e7e505648dde326810fa34af207f43cd7a5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Cumulative Frequencies: 10, 22, 40, 60, 80

⇒ Total Frequency **N = 80**

⇒ **N/2 = 80 / 2 = 40**

⇒ The cumulative frequency just greater than or equal to 40 is 40, which belongs to class **200−220**.

⇒ L = 200, cfₚ = 22, fₘ = 18, h = 20

⇒ Median = 200 + [(40 − 22) / 18] × 20

⇒ Median = 200 + [18 / 18] × 20

⇒ Median = 200 + 20 = 220

**∴ The correct answer is 220.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

The relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode is: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Median for Grouped Data

Median is the value that divides the data into two equal halves. For grouped data, it is calculated using the interpolation formula based on the **Median Class**.

Mean of Grouped Data

Mean (μ) = Σ(fᵢ × xᵢ) / Σfᵢ, where xᵢ is the class mark (mid-point) of each interval.</p

questions.question: The median of the observations 60, 43, 24, 61, 72, 26, 39, 62, 49, 95 and 38 is:

Arrange the 11 observations in **ascending order**: 24, 26, 38, 39, 43, 49, 60, 61, 62, 72, 95.

Since the number of observations (**N = 11**) is **odd**, the **median** is the exact **middle term**.

**Median** = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th term = **6th term**.

**Formula Used:**

When **N** is **odd**:

**Median** = ((N + 1) ÷ 2)th observation (after arranging in **ascending order**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3b9579381e9f11b4e47eaafbb6a53ba2f02d7e0a06176eea0ba1dba66bd97e77.png]

⇒ 24, 26, 38, 39, 43, 49, 60, 61, 62, 72, 95

⇒ **Median** = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th term

⇒ **Median** = (12 ÷ 2)th term

⇒ **Median** = **6th term**

⇒ **6th term** = **49**

Thus, the **median** of the given observations is **49**.

**Explanation of incorrect options:**

⇒ **Option (3) 60** is the 7th term, which is not the exact middle term.

questions.question: What is the significance of pipelining in CPU architecture?

options.text: Increases clock speed using multiple cores
Executes multiple instructions simultaneously by overlapping stages

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Executes multiple instructions simultaneously by overlapping stages**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pipelining** is a technique used in CPU architecture to improve instruction throughput by executing multiple instructions simultaneously in a staggered manner.
 
• It divides the execution of an instruction into multiple stages (such as fetch, decode, execute, memory access, and write-back) that operate in parallel.
 
• Each stage of the pipeline processes a different instruction, enabling the CPU to work on several instructions at the same time.
 
• Pipelining significantly enhances overall performance by increasing instruction throughput, not clock speed.
 
• This technique is widely used in modern processors to optimize efficiency in executing complex operations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Instruction Pipeline Stages:**

 
 
• The pipeline is typically divided into stages like Fetch, Decode, Execute, Memory Access, and Write-Back.
 
• Each stage performs a specific task, and all stages operate simultaneously on different instructions.
 
 
 
• **Hazards in Pipelining:**
 
 
• Hazards are potential issues that can disrupt the smooth execution of instructions in a pipeline.
 
• Types of hazards include Data Hazards (dependency on previous instructions), Control Hazards (branching or jumping), and Structural Hazards (resource conflicts).
 
 
 
• **Superscalar Architecture:**
 
 
• Modern CPUs often combine pipelining with superscalar execution, enabling multiple pipelines to operate in parallel.
 
• This further boosts the number of instructions executed per clock cycle.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Pipelining:**
 
 
• Pipelining improves throughput but does not reduce the execution time of a single instruction.
 
• Performance gains can be affected by hazards or variations in instruction execution times.

questions.question: A seller marks their goods 45% above the cost price. On customer demand, they offer a 60% reduction on the bills. What percentage of profit or loss does the seller make?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Here, markup percentage **a = +45%** and discount percentage **b = −60%**.

Net change = 45 − 60 + (45 × (−60)) ÷ 100

Net change = −15 − 2700 ÷ 100 = −15 − 27 = **−42%**.

The negative sign indicates a **loss of 42%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 42% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Markup = 45% above CP, Discount = 60% on MP.
**Formulas:** MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 | Loss% = (CP − SP) ÷ CP × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0a07e0c8738a54dbf19295fec919a1a7c05355cd98b9f5d1c5cf449c6580bbd.png] 

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** be 100.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 45% of 100 = 145.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = MP − 60% of MP = 145 × (40 ÷ 100) = 58.

⇒ Loss = CP − SP = 100 − 58 = 42.

⇒ **Loss Percentage** = (42 ÷ 100) × 100 = 42%.

**∴ The correct answer is 42% loss.**

The final profit or loss depends on the cumulative effect of the initial **markup** and the subsequent **discount** offered.</p

questions.question: The side AB and AC of △ABC are produced to points D and E, respectively. The bisectors of ∠CBD and ∠BCE meet at P. If ∠A = 84∘, then the measure of P is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The angle formed by the **external bisectors** of two angles of a triangle is given by the formula:

∠P = 90° − ∠A/2

Given ∠A = 84°

∠P = 90° − 84°/2 = 90° − 42° = 48°

**∴ The correct answer is 48°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

∠A = 84°

**Formula Used:**

In ▵ABC, if sides AB and AC are produced to D and E, and the bisectors of exterior angles ∠CBD and ∠BCE meet at P, then ∠BPC = 90° − ∠A/2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/afc752c40eddfa6c38369cbc191acce463263c0cf45579765241c44cbd13f463.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In **▵ABC**, the sides AB and AC are produced to points D and E respectively.

⇒ The bisectors of **exterior angles** ∠CBD and ∠BCE meet at point P.

⇒ Point P is the **ex-center** of the triangle opposite to vertex A.

⇒ The measure of ∠P is given by the relation: ∠P = 90° − ∠A/2

⇒ Substituting the value of ∠A = 84°:

⇒ ∠P = 90° − (84° / 2)

⇒ ∠P = 90° − 42°

⇒ ∠P = 48°

**∴ The correct answer is 48°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Incenter Angle

The angle formed by the intersection of **internal angle bisectors** (Incenter I) is ∠BIC = 90° + ∠A/2.

Exterior Angle Theorem

An **exterior angle** of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles: ∠CBD = ∠A + ∠C.

Ex-center Definition

The **ex-center** is the point where the bisector of one interior angle and the bisectors of the other two exterior angles intersect.</p

questions.question: The average score of 10 players was initially recorded as 55. However, it was later discovered that a score of 84 had been mistakenly read as 48. Determine the correct average score.

Net change in **total score** = Correct score − Wrong score = 84 − 48 = +36.

Change in **average** = Net change ÷ Number of players = 36 ÷ 10 = +3.6.

Correct average = Initial average + Change in average = 55 + 3.6 = 58.6.

**∴ The correct answer is 58.6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial average of **10 players** = 55

Incorrectly recorded score = 48

Actual correct score = 84

**Formula Used:**

Average = Total Sum ÷ Number of items

Correct Sum = (Initial Average × n) − Wrong Value + Correct Value

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Total Sum = 10 × 55 = 550

⇒ Correct Total Sum = 550 − 48 + 84

⇒ Correct Average = 586 ÷ 10

Average Correction Rule

When one or more values are incorrectly recorded, the new average can be calculated using New Average = Old Average + [(Correct Value − Incorrect Value) ÷ Total Number of Items].

Net Deviation

The sum of deviations of all observations from their **arithmetic mean** is always zero. In correction problems, the net deviation is simply the difference between the correct and incorrect values.

Combined Average

If two groups with n₁ and n₂ items have averages a₁ and a₂, the combined average is (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: A person saves 30% of his income. If his expenditure is ₹560, then his income (in ₹) is:

__
 
• The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1978 reduced the number of Fundamental Rights from seven to six.
 
• The amendment abolished the Fundamental Right to Property under Article 31 and moved it to the category of legal rights under Article 300A.
 
• The Fundamental Rights now include: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
• This amendment was enacted during the Janata Party government to reverse some provisions introduced during the Emergency period (1975-1977).

• **Fundamental Rights:**

 
 
• These are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution and are essential for the development of individuals and the protection of their liberties.
 
• They are justiciable, meaning individuals can approach the courts for their enforcement.
 
• Originally, there were seven Fundamental Rights, but the Right to Property was removed as a Fundamental Right by the 44th Amendment.
 
 
 
• **44th Constitutional Amendment Act:**
 
 
• Enacted in 1978, it was introduced to undo the excesses of the 42nd Amendment passed during the Emergency.
 
• It aimed to restore the balance between the executive, legislature, and judiciary.
 
• It ensured that the proclamation of Emergency required stricter conditions and safeguarded citizens' rights during such times.
 
 
 
• **Right to Property:**
 
 
• Initially a Fundamental Right under Article 31, it guaranteed protection against arbitrary state actions regarding property.
 
• The 44th Amendment moved it to Article 300A, making it a legal right, thereby allowing the state to impose reasonable restrictions.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Amendment:**
 
 
• It marked a shift from authoritarian governance toward strengthening democratic principles.
 
• It provided safeguards to prevent misuse of constitutional provisions in the future.

• **Article 342** pertains to the specification of Scheduled Tribes, unrelated to language provisions.
 
• The Official Language Act of **1963** further elaborates on the use of Hindi and English in official communications, ensuring linguistic inclusivity.
 
• The idea behind these constitutional provisions is to promote national integration while respecting linguistic diversity across India.

questions.question: The addition of H⁺ ions to the equilibrium CH₃COOH ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺ will:
questions.solution:

__
 
• Adding H⁺ ions to the equilibrium system CH₃COOH ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺ increases the concentration of H⁺ ions.
 
• According to Le Chatelier's Principle, the system will shift to counteract the disturbance, favoring the reverse reaction.
 
• The reverse reaction converts CH₃COO⁻ and H⁺ into CH₃COOH, thereby shifting the equilibrium to the left.
 
• This adjustment decreases the dissociation of acetic acid (CH₃COOH) and increases its concentration in the solution.
 
• The equilibrium shift restores balance by reducing the excess H⁺ ions added to the system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Le Chatelier's Principle:**

 
 
• It states that if a dynamic equilibrium is disturbed by changing conditions, the system responds to counteract the change and restore equilibrium.
 
• In this case, adding H⁺ ions shifts the equilibrium to reduce their concentration.
 
 
 
• **Acetic Acid (CH₃COOH):**
 
 
• A weak acid that partially dissociates in water into CH₃COO⁻ and H⁺ ions.
 
• The dissociation is reversible, allowing equilibrium to be established between the reactants and products.
 
 
 
• **Weak Acids:**
 
 
• Weak acids do not fully ionize in water; only a small fraction dissociates into ions.
 
• Examples include acetic acid (CH₃COOH), citric acid, and formic acid.
 
 
 
• **Equilibrium Constants:**
 
 
• The equilibrium constant (Kₐ) for weak acids measures the extent of dissociation of the acid.
 
• For acetic acid, Kₐ is small, indicating limited dissociation in aqueous solutions.
 
 
 
• **Effect of Adding Reactants or Products:**
 
 
• Adding reactants or products disturbs the equilibrium, prompting a shift to re-establish balance.
 
• In this case, adding H⁺ ions favors the reverse reaction to reduce their concentration.

questions.question: The period from 1905 to 1917 is known as the "Extremist Phase" in the Indian National Movement. Which of the following leaders was NOT associated with the extremist ideology during this time?

The correct answer is __**Gopal Krishna Gokhale**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a prominent leader of the **Moderate faction** in the Indian National Movement, advocating gradual reforms and constitutional methods.
 
• He opposed the extremist ideology led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai during the "Extremist Phase" (1905–1917).
 
• Gokhale founded the **Servants of India Society** in 1905 to promote education, social reform, and dialogue with the British government.
 
• Unlike extremists, Gokhale believed in cooperation with the British government and rejected aggressive methods like boycott and swadeshi.

• Lala Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Bal Gangadhar Tilak were the three main leaders of the extremist faction, collectively referred to as the "Lal-Bal-Pal" trio.
 
• They advocated swadeshi, boycott of British goods, and self-reliance to achieve independence.
 
• Their methods included mass protests, public mobilization, and stronger resistance against colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Moderates vs. Extremists:**
 
 
• Moderates, led by leaders like Gokhale, relied on petitions, resolutions, and constitutional reforms.
 
• Extremists adopted a more radical approach, emphasizing direct action and mass participation.
 
• The ideological split became evident during the Surat session of Congress in 1907.
 
 
 
• **Swadeshi Movement:**
 
 
• The Swadeshi Movement was launched in 1905 as a response to the partition of Bengal.
 
• It involved boycotting British goods and promoting indigenous industries.
 
• Extremists played a key role in popularizing swadeshi, while moderates supported it cautiously.
 
 
 
• **Servants of India Society:**
 
 
• Founded by Gokhale in 1905, the society aimed to train Indians in social service and nation-building.
 
• It focused on education, poverty alleviation, and improving governance.
 
• It became a significant platform for nurturing future leaders committed to Gandhian ideals.

questions.question: Which of the following abbreviations represents a volatile memory technology commonly used for the primary working memory in personal computers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**DRAM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **DRAM (Dynamic Random Access Memory)** is a type of volatile memory that is widely used as the primary working memory (RAM) in personal computers.
 
• It requires constant refreshing of data multiple times per second to retain information, making it "dynamic."
 
• DRAM is faster than traditional storage devices such as hard drives but slower than SRAM (Static Random Access Memory).
 
• It is cost-effective and offers high storage density, which is why it is the preferred choice for system memory in most PCs and laptops.
 
• DRAM modules are available in various forms, such as DDR (Double Data Rate) versions like DDR3, DDR4, and DDR5, which enhance speed and efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Volatile Memory:**

 
 
• Volatile memory requires a constant power supply to retain data. When the power is turned off, all data is lost.
 
• Examples include DRAM and SRAM, used mainly for temporary data storage during system operations.
 
 
 
• **SRAM (Static Random Access Memory):**
 
 
• SRAM is another type of volatile memory that does not require constant refreshing to retain data.
 
• It is faster but more expensive and less dense compared to DRAM, making it suitable for cache memory in CPUs.
 
 
 
• **DDR (Double Data Rate) DRAM:**
 
 
• DDR memory improves the performance of DRAM by transferring data on both the rising and falling edges of the clock signal.
 
• DDR4 and DDR5 are the most commonly used DRAM types in modern computers, offering higher bandwidth and lower power consumption.
 
 
 
• **Non-Volatile Memory:**
 
 
• Non-volatile memory retains data even when the power is turned off, making it ideal for long-term data storage.
 
• Examples include flash memory, SSDs, and ROM (Read-Only Memory).
 
 
 
• **CMOS (Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor):**
 
 
• CMOS is a low-power semiconductor technology used for constructing integrated circuits.
 
• It is commonly used for small amounts of memory in devices like BIOS to store system settings.

questions.question: If a² + b² = 169, a times b = 10, and a > b, find (a - b)/(a + b)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Directly calculate the values of the squared expressions:

(a − b)² = (a² + b²) − 2ab = 169 − 20 = 149

(a + b)² = (a² + b²) + 2ab = 169 + 20 = 189

Required Ratio = √((a − b)² / (a + b)²) = √(149/189)

**∴ The correct answer is √(149/189).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a² + b² = 169

ab = 10

a > b

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e679230b1dd97ba8004d610820f82b641e4545798f8f19a051b04e7e85d44bd4.png] 

**Formula Used:**

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

**Calculations:**

⇒ (a − b)² = 169 − 2(10)

⇒ (a − b)² = 169 − 20 = 149

⇒ a − b = √149 (Since a > b)

⇒ (a + b)² = 169 + 2(10)

⇒ (a + b)² = 169 + 20 = 189

⇒ a + b = √189

⇒ Ratio = (a − b) / (a + b) = √149 / √189

⇒ Ratio = √(149/189)

**∴ The correct answer is √(149/189).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Algebraic Identities

Basic expansion: (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab.

Difference of Squares

(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².

Relation between Squares

(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.</p

questions.question: In the architecture of a Central Processing Unit (CPU), which statement accurately distinguishes the function of the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) from that of the Control Unit (CU)?

options.text: ALU decodes instructions, while CU handles data storage tasks.
CU executes arithmetic operations, and ALU controls program instructions.
CU interacts directly with peripheral devices, and ALU stores temporary data
ALU handles calculations and logic functions; CU manages instruction flow and coordination.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ALU handles calculations and logic functions; CU manages instruction flow and coordination.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)** performs arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, etc.) and logical operations (AND, OR, NOT, etc.).
 
• The **Control Unit (CU)** directs the operation of the CPU by interpreting program instructions and coordinating the flow of data between the CPU, memory, and peripherals.
 
• While the ALU focuses on computation, the CU ensures the proper sequencing and execution of instructions.
 
• The CU does not perform calculations; its role is purely supervisory and organizational within the CPU architecture.
 
• The ALU and CU are integral components of the CPU, working together to ensure efficient data processing and program execution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Processing Unit (CPU):**

 
 
• The CPU is the primary component of a computer responsible for executing instructions.
 
• It consists of three main parts: the ALU, CU, and registers.
 
• Registers provide temporary storage for quick data access during processing.
 
 
 
• **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU):**
 
 
• It is a fundamental part of the CPU that performs all arithmetic and logical operations.
 
• Examples of arithmetic operations include addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
 
• Logical operations include comparisons, such as greater than, less than, and equality.
 
 
 
• **Control Unit (CU):**
 
 
• It acts as the "brain" of the CPU, ensuring instruction execution in the correct sequence.
 
• The CU decodes instructions from programs and sends control signals to other components.
 
• It manages communication between the CPU and input/output devices.
 
 
 
• **CPU Architecture:**
 
 
• Modern CPUs use a combination of ALU, CU, and cache memory for efficient data processing.
 
• Multi-core CPUs contain multiple ALUs and CUs to enhance parallel processing and overall performance.
 
• Instruction pipelining is a technique used to improve the execution speed of a CPU.

questions.question: The maximum number of Buddhist stupas had been built by which of the following rulers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ashoka, the third emperor of the Maurya Dynasty**, is renowned for constructing the maximum number of Buddhist stupas across India.
 
• He built stupas to house and honor the sacred relics of Lord Buddha, promoting Buddhism as a state religion after his conversion post the Kalinga War.
 
• Ashoka is credited with constructing **84,000 stupas**, as per Buddhist texts like the "Ashokavadana."
 
• Famous stupas such as the **Sanchi Stupa** and Barabar caves were built under his patronage, symbolizing the spread of Buddhist teachings.
 
• These stupas served both as religious monuments and centers for Buddhist education and community gathering.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Buddhist Stupa:**

 
 
• A stupa is a dome-shaped structure that serves as a Buddhist shrine and symbolizes enlightenment, the path to nirvana, and the Buddha’s relics.
 
• The stupa design is rooted in ancient Indian funerary traditions, representing the Buddha's parinirvana (final release from the cycle of rebirth).
 
 
 
• **Ashoka’s Role in Buddhism:**
 
 
• Ashoka embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War, where he witnessed the immense suffering caused by the conflict.
 
• He convened the **Third Buddhist Council** to purify and systematize Buddhist teachings and sent missionaries to other regions to propagate Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Sanchi Stupa:**
 
 
• Located in Madhya Pradesh, it is one of the oldest stone structures in India and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• It was commissioned by Ashoka and contains relics of the Buddha.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka’s Edicts:**
 
 
• Ashoka’s inscriptions, engraved on pillars and rocks, emphasize moral values, non-violence, and the spread of Dhamma (righteousness).
 
• The famous Ashoka Pillars, including the one at Sarnath, symbolize his commitment to Buddhism and ethical governance.

questions.question: Rishika travels a certain distance at a speed of 52 km/hr and double the earlier distance at 39 km/hr. She then returns to the starting point through the same route. If her average speed for the entire journey is 56 km/h, then what is her speed (in km/hr) for the return journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial distance be **156 km** (LCM of 52 and 39). Total distance for outward journey = 156 + 2 × 156 = 468 km.

Outward time = (156 ÷ 52) + (312 ÷ 39) = 3 + 8 = **11 hours**.

Total journey distance (out + return) = 468 × 2 = **936 km**. Total time = 936 ÷ 56 = **117/7 hours**.

Return time = 117/7 − 11 = (117 − 77)/7 = **40/7 hours**.

Return Speed = 468 ÷ (40/7) = (468 × 7) ÷ 40 = 3276 ÷ 40 = **81.9 km/hr**.

**∴ The correct answer is 81.9 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9306f383fe0a30e5e9ef0c48ed871b2e6b2bc4354a0a68be9a8f41bd088ca4e3.png] 

**Given:** Speed 1 = 52 km/h, Distance 1 = D; Speed 2 = 39 km/h, Distance 2 = 2D; Average Speed = 56 km/h.

**Formula:** Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Total Distance = D + 2D + 3D (Return) = 6D

⇒ Total Time = (D/52) + (2D/39) + (3D/v)

⇒ 56 = 6D / [(D/52) + (2D/39) + (3D/v)]

⇒ 56 = 6 / [(3/156) + (8/156) + (3/v)]

⇒ 56 = 6 / [11/156 + 3/v]

⇒ 11/156 + 3/v = 6/56 = 3/28

⇒ 3/v = 3/28 − 11/156 = (3 × 39 − 11 × 7) / 1092 = (117 − 77) / 1092

⇒ 3/v = 40 / 1092

⇒ v = (1092 × 3) / 40 = 3276 / 40 = 81.9 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 81.9 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

When two equal distances are covered at speeds u and v, Average Speed = 2uv / (u + v). For three equal distances, it is 3uvw / (uv + vw + wu).

Weighted Average Speed

If distances d₁, d₂,... are covered at speeds v₁, v₂,..., Average Speed = (Σdᵢ) / (Σdᵢ/vᵢ).

Time & Distance Relation

Distance = Speed × Time. If distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (v₁/v₂ = t₂/t₁).</p

questions.question: Which ruler of the Delhi Sultanate was associated with the expedition to Bhilsa (Vidisha) in AD 1292?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alauddin Khilji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Alauddin Khilji, the second ruler of the Khilji dynasty (1296–1316), is associated with the expedition to Bhilsa (modern-day Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh) in AD 1292.
 
• Bhilsa was a prominent cultural and religious center during the medieval period, known for its strategic location and wealth.
 
• This expedition aimed to subdue the region and establish control over its resources as part of Alauddin Khilji's expansionist policies.
 
• Alauddin's military campaigns were instrumental in consolidating the Delhi Sultanate’s rule and extending its influence over central India.
 
• The Bhilsa expedition was a precursor to his later, more significant campaigns in the Deccan and other regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alauddin Khilji’s Military Campaigns**

 
 
• He is known for his conquests in Gujarat, Ranthambore, Chittor, and the Deccan, which expanded the Delhi Sultanate’s territorial reach significantly.
 
• His campaigns were marked by meticulous planning, strong military leadership, and efficient resource management.
 
 
 
• **Bhilsa (Vidisha)**
 
 
• An ancient city located in Madhya Pradesh, Vidisha was historically significant for its Buddhist monuments and the famous Sanchi Stupa nearby.
 
• It was a center of trade, culture, and religion during the medieval period, attracting the attention of invading rulers.
 
 
 
• **The Khilji Dynasty**
 
 
• Established by Jalaluddin Khilji in 1290, the dynasty ruled the Delhi Sultanate until 1320.
 
• Alauddin Khilji is considered its most prominent ruler, known for his administrative reforms and military strategies.
 
 
 
• **Administrative and Economic Reforms of Alauddin Khilji**
 
 
• He introduced market control policies to stabilize prices and prevent hoarding.
 
• Land revenue reforms ensured a steady income for the state while curbing the power of local chieftains.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Alauddin Khilji**

questions.question: The sum of five numbers is 655. The average of the first two numbers is 77 and the third number is 101. Find the average of the remaining two numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Sum of last two numbers** = Total Sum − (Sum of first two + Third number)

Sum of last two = 655 − (77 × 2 + 101)

Sum of last two = 655 − (154 + 101) = 655 − 255 = 400

**Required Average** = 400 ÷ 2 = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Sum of 5 numbers** = 655

**Average of 1st and 2ⁿd number** = 77

**Value of 3rd number** = 101

**Formula Used:**

Sum = Average × Number of observations

Average = Sum ÷ Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c3fcaa6755622fe8c8aea3e6a2799ab101898355a7fb95161d8d58756f89bb61.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of first two numbers = 77 × 2 = 154

⇒ Sum of first three numbers = 154 + 101 = 255

⇒ Sum of remaining two numbers = Total Sum − Sum of first three numbers

⇒ Sum of remaining two numbers = 655 − 255 = 400

⇒ Average of remaining two numbers = 400 ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Definition of Average

Average is the **central value** of a set of data, calculated by dividing the total sum of values by the number of values.

Properties of Averages

If every number in a set is increased or decreased by a constant **'k'**, the average also increases or decreases by **'k'**.

Weighted Average

When groups have different sizes, the combined average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: The curved surface area of a cylinder is half of its total surface area. If its height is 12 cm, then find its diameter (in cm).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given: **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = 1/2 × **Total Surface Area (TSA)**

For a **cylinder**, if **CSA** = 1/2 **TSA**, then **2πrh** = 1/2 × 2πr(h + r)

This simplifies to **2h = h + r** ⇒ **h = r**

Given **height (h)** = 12 cm, therefore **radius (r)** = 12 cm

**Diameter** = 2 × r = 2 × 12 = 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Height (h)** of the cylinder = 12 cm

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = 1/2 × **Total Surface Area (TSA)**

**Formula Used:**

**CSA** of cylinder = 2πrh

**TSA** of cylinder = 2πr(h + r)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/affa048ca6b4c21009d51aab8ef9000aca45ee7da55215f77b3578c6c8de9fec.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2πrh = 1/2 × [2πr(h + r)]

⇒ 2πrh = πr(h + r)

⇒ 2h = h + r

⇒ r = h

⇒ r = 12 cm

⇒ **Diameter (d)** = 2 × r

⇒ d = 2 × 12 = 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cylinder

The amount of space occupied by the cylinder is given by V = πr²h.

Base Area of Cylinder

The area of the circular base or top is A = πr². TSA is the sum of CSA and twice the Base Area.

Relation between Diameter and Radius

The diameter is the longest chord of the circular base and is twice the radius (d = 2r).</p

questions.question: Find a single discount (rounded up to two decimal places) equal to three consecutive discounts of 26%, 29% and 2%.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Discount for 26% and 29% = 26 + 29 − (26 × 29) ÷ 100 = 55 − 7.54 = 47.46%.

Now, combine 47.46% with 2% discount = 47.46 + 2 − (47.46 × 2) ÷ 100.

⇒ 49.46 − 0.9492 = 48.5108%.

Rounding up to two decimal places, we get 48.51%.

**∴ The correct answer is 48.51%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Three consecutive discounts: **d₁ = 26%**, **d₂ = 29%**, and **d₃ = 2%**.
Formulas: **Net SP = MP × (100 − d₁)% × (100 − d₂)% × (100 − d₃)%** | **Single Discount% = (MP − SP) ÷ MP × 100**.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2277b99a546dc882c8125320e856fc498fd750504a65e48867d9fd7136e14c5.png] 
⇒ Let the **Marked Price (MP)** be 100.
⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 × (74 ÷ 100) × (71 ÷ 100) × (98 ÷ 100).
⇒ SP = 100 × 0.74 × 0.71 × 0.98 = 51.4892.
⇒ **Single Equivalent Discount** = MP − SP = 100 − 51.4892 = 48.5108%.
⇒ Rounded to two decimal places = 48.51%.

**∴ The correct answer is 48.51%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two or more discounts are applied one after another, they are called **successive discounts**. The total effective discount is always less than the simple sum of individual discounts.

Formula for Two Discounts

For two discounts a% and b%, the **Single Equivalent Discount** = [a + b − (ab ÷ 100)]%.</p

questions.question: Ramesh can complete a piece of work alone in 16 days and Suresh can complete the same piece of work alone in 10 days. They started the work together, but Ramesh had to leave 4 days before the completion of the work. In how many days will the work get completed?

Total days = Adjusted Work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 100 ÷ (5 + 8) = 100/13 days.

⇒ 5 × (x − 4) + 8 × x = 80

⇒ 5x − 20 + 8x = 80

⇒ 13x = 100

⇒ x = 100/13 = 7(9/13) days

**∴ The correct answer is 7(9/13) days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Leaving Early vs Joining Late

If a person leaves **'n' days before completion**, add (n × efficiency) to total work. If a person joins **'n' days late**, it does not change the total work units but reduces their active time.

Pipes and Cisterns

Similar logic applies where efficiency of an **outlet pipe** is taken as negative, while an **inlet pipe** is positive.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the **actual work done** by each individual (Efficiency × Time).</p

questions.question: Which physiographic feature lies parallel to the Shiwaliks and is about 8-16 km wide?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhabar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bhabar** is a narrow belt of 8-16 km in width lying parallel to the southern edge of the Shiwalik hills.
 
• This region is characterized by coarse alluvial deposits made up of pebbles and boulders brought down by the rivers descending from the Himalayas.
 
• It is marked by a high porosity of soil, causing streams and rivers to disappear and flow underground.
 
• The Bhabar zone is unsuitable for cultivation due to its rocky terrain and coarse soil texture.
 
• This belt serves as a transition zone between the hilly areas of the Shiwaliks and the fertile plains of the Terai region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shiwalik Hills:**

 
 
• Also known as the Outer Himalayas, the Shiwalik hills are the southernmost range of the Himalayas.
 
• They are composed of unconsolidated sediments, making them prone to erosion.
 
• The width of this range varies between 10 and 50 km, and its altitude ranges from 600 to 1500 meters.
 
 
 
• **Terai Region:**
 
 
• The Terai is a low-lying, marshy region lying south of the Bhabar belt.
 
• Unlike the Bhabar, the streams in this region re-emerge on the surface, making the area highly fertile and suitable for agriculture.
 
• The Terai is also home to rich biodiversity and dense forests, such as those found in Jim Corbett National Park.
 
 
 
• **Doab:**
 
 
• A doab refers to the fertile land between two converging rivers.
 
• For example, the Ganga-Yamuna Doab is one of the most agriculturally productive regions in India.
 
 
 
• **Alluvial Deposits:**
 
 
• Alluvium is a loose soil or sediment deposited by rivers, typically consisting of sand, silt, and clay.
 
• Regions like the Indo-Gangetic plain owe their fertility to alluvial deposits brought by Himalayan rivers.

questions.question: Which of the following architectures was built by Aurangzeb?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bibi-ka-Maqbara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bibi-ka-Maqbara** is a mausoleum located in Aurangabad, Maharashtra, and was built by Aurangzeb in memory of his first wife, Dilras Banu Begum.
 
• The construction of Bibi-ka-Maqbara began in 1651 and was completed in 1661 under the supervision of Aurangzeb's son, Azam Shah.
 
• It is often referred to as the "Taj of the Deccan" due to its resemblance to the Taj Mahal, although it is less grand in scale and detailing.
 
• The architecture was designed by Ata-ullah, the son of Ustad Ahmad Lahauri, who was the chief architect of the Taj Mahal.
 
• The structure is primarily made of marble and features intricate carvings, showcasing a blend of Mughal architectural styles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aurangzeb's Architectural Legacy:**

 
 
• Aurangzeb was not as prolific a patron of architecture as his predecessors; he focused more on military campaigns and administration.
 
• Bibi-ka-Maqbara is one of the few significant architectural projects commissioned during his reign.
 
• Unlike the Taj Mahal, Aurangzeb restricted excessive expenditure on monuments, reflecting his austere approach.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Architecture:**
 
 
• Mughal architecture is a blend of Islamic, Persian, Turkish, and Indian architectural styles, characterized by domes, arches, minarets, and intricate ornamentation.
 
• Prominent examples include the Taj Mahal, Humayun’s Tomb, and Jama Masjid.
 
 
 
• **Other Monuments Built by Aurangzeb:**
 
 
• Aurangzeb built several mosques, such as the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore and the Moti Masjid in Delhi.
 
• These structures were more functional and less ornate compared to those built by earlier Mughal emperors.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Taj Mahal:**
 
 
• Bibi-ka-Maqbara’s resemblance to the Taj Mahal highlights the influence of Shah Jahan’s architectural style on Aurangzeb’s era.
 
• However, the materials used and the scale of construction were comparatively modest due to budgetary constraints imposed by Aurangzeb.
